About Event

WHAT IS re:AGENT

re:AGENT is a two-day build weekend focused on the infrastructure scientific agents still need: better datasets, sharper tools, and reliable ways to evaluate their work. Participants will use Paperclip , Proto , Claude , and other scientific AI tools to build systems that can take on real scientific problems and produce results worth trusting.
Paperclip turns papers, datasets, clinical trials, and biological databases into an agent-native workspace that AI systems can search, synthesize, and build upon. Proto is a design framework and infrastructure layer for generative biology, allowing builders to combine AI models and search for DNA, RNA, or protein sequences that satisfy custom criteria.
The weekend brings together engineers, scientists, computational biologists, founders, and AI researchers. Projects might include assembling a research-ready dataset that would be impractical to create by hand, along with the analysis needed to show that its findings are real. Others might involve designing a new biological system to a defined specification and testing whether it holds up against existing evidence.
The aim is not just to accelerate existing workflows, but to create the tools, datasets, and evaluation methods that make entirely new scientific questions and experiments possible.
READY TO BUILD?

If you're excited about the future of AI, agents and scientific discovery, we'll see you there...
We will close applications on Thursday, 30th of July, 12 PM PST. Spots will be confirmed on Friday, 31st of July.
WHO SHOULD ATTEND
People with the questions: scientists of all stripes. Wet lab, computational, clinical, industry. Biology, biochemistry, biophysics, chemistry, structural. Anyone with a real problem, ideally a real dataset, and the judgment to tell right from wrong results.
People who build for a living: ML engineers, software developers, and agent builders who can take a half-formed scientific problem and ship something that runs by Sunday.
No prior AI expertise required. Participants are welcome at all levels.

Tracks
Track A: Build an AI Scientist
Build an AI agent that can carry out a defined scientific or drug-development workflow from start to finish. It should gather evidence, use relevant tools or databases, generate and test hypotheses, produce a structured output, and make its reasoning easy to inspect. This could mean reasoning over experimental data, scientific literature, or learned representations like protein embeddings. Examples include a virtual FDA reviewer, toxicology agent, clinical trial designer, experimental planning agent, or a protein-discovery agent that generates and tests hypotheses over protein embeddings and structural features.
Track B: Build a Dataset or Meta-Analysis

What have you always wanted the literature to tell you, but could never read fast enough to find out? Draft the queries, run them across thousands of papers, sharpen and re-run until the results hold the specific pieces you care about. Then the real work: find the pattern in what you assembled that no single paper could show you, and demo that.
Track C: Build the Biological Design

Assemble a pipeline that designs biology to a spec you choose, from a single protein up to a multi-gene system. You set the constraints; the models generate candidates and evolve them toward something that could hold up in a real cell. Could the literature reveal the most promising design space for a generative model to explore? What you demo is the new biological design you made — the sequence or system that didn't exist before you built it.
Or come with a different project of your own.
Prizes will be awarded.

FAQs
Do I need a biology background or an AI background to participate?

No. We're looking for engineers with no life sciences experience as well as individuals who are in life sciences. One is helpful, but you don’t need both. The best teams usually pair technical builders with someone who knows the science.
Do I need a team before applying?
No. You can apply as a team, but you don’t have to. You can apply solo, and you'll meet potential teammates at the kickoff event.
What will I have access to during the hackathon?

Free Paperclip API access, access to Proto , Claude API credits, and compute and credits from our sponsors.
Is there a cost to attend?
The event is free to attend. Food, drinks, and compute are covered .
What happens to what I build afterward?

You keep it. Teams are free to open-source, continue building, or spin their project into something bigger.

48 hours of hands-on building and prototyping

One year ago, we opened a hub where AI builders could show up for each other. On September 22, we're celebrating everyone who did — and everything that got built because of it!
Join us for a night of real conversations about AI, community, and what comes next. We will have:
A panel with AI builders, community leaders, and founders moderated by Jeremiah Owyang

Builders who came here for a hackathon weekend and are still shipping

Stories from startups who built their companies right inside these walls

Plus food, music, a photo booth, community trading cards, and more!

The SVAI Hub was built on one conviction: the best AI doesn't get built in isolation. It gets built by communities — developers leveling up together, founders stress-testing ideas with peers, researchers colliding with practitioners in the same room. In September 2025, we opened our space in the heart of Silicon Valley. Not for vendor pitches. Not for product demos. For the conversations and connections that actually move the field forward.
One year in, the numbers tell part of the story:
100+ AI community events

10,000+ developers, founders, and executives through our doors

6 hackathons that launched real projects and real careers

The numbers tell part of the story. The conversations tell the rest.
Come for the milestone. Stay for the momentum, connections and networking!

The Humans at the Mic 🎤
Built Here. Still Building. — Hackathon Winners Spotlight
Victoria Duan — OrchestrAI | Llama Lounge Hackathon, 1st Place
Victoria built the core agentic framework for OrchestrAI, took first place, and hasn't stopped building since — she's now deep in AI developer tooling and exploring how AI changes the way software gets made.

Abraham Bhatti , Rishit Sai & Yash Sanghvi — ToolForge | Llama Lounge Hackathon, 2nd Place
They built an AI agent that creates its own tools, won together, kept competing together, and are now in early customer discovery to turn it into a real product.

Panel: Build Together — The Advantage of Community in AI
Jeremiah Owyang (moderator) — VC at Blitzscaling Ventures, global keynote speaker, and founder of Llama Lounge — the Bay Area's most popular AI startup event series, drawing hundreds of founders, investors, and builders every month.

Grace Gong — Founder of Smart Venture Media, host of two top-ranked VC podcasts (Smart Venture Podcast and Venture with Grace), angel investor, and founder of Smart AI Summits — a LinkedIn Top Voice in Finance with a front-row seat to where AI and venture capital intersect.

Swagata Ashwani — AI Tech Lead & Manager at Boomi, co-lead of the Women in Data SF chapter, and a LinkedIn Top Voice in AI — a technical builder who brings a practitioner's view of how community helps people stay sharp, learn faster, and grow with AI.

Sheena Tu — Co-founder of TechEquity Ai, a Silicon Valley nonprofit expanding access to AI through practical learning, industry collaboration, and community-driven programs, including forums, workshops, hackathons, and its annual Summit, reaching thousands of participants across the Bay Area and beyond.

Startup Showcase — Stories from the Hub
Every week, a group of startup founders work from the SVAI Hub. Two of those companies will share what they're building, how this community changed how they built it, and where they are now — in three minutes, no pitch deck.
Ivan Lee — Founder and CEO, Datasaur
Ivan sold his first startup to Yahoo, built AI systems at Apple, and has spent the last seven years focused on the problem most AI vendors don't want to talk about: what happens to your data after you hand it over. At Datasaur, he helps enterprises in financial services, healthcare, legal, and government deploy fully air-gapped private LLMs — frontier-model capability, zero data leaving the building. His version of the future: the most powerful AI is the one you fully control.

Mayank Kumar — Founding AI Engineer, DeepTempo
Over the last decade Mayank has built safety-critical systems, trained large-scale AI models, and served communities through his social entrepreneurial ventures. At DeepTempo, he is building the Intelligent Defense Platform. Attackers are already using AI to move faster than the teams defending against them, and those teams are working with tools built for a slower era. The platform is his answer to that gap: LogLM is the intelligence layer, a foundation model that learns what normal activity looks like across many kinds of security data and flags what does not belong, and Vigil is the investigation layer, an open source system where AI agents take those signals and work out what actually happened. His bet for the next few years: defenders need to operate at machine speed too.
